text.tspan:
Income inequality vs. GDP per capita
1985 to 2024

The
Gini coefficient
measures inequality on a scale from 0 to 1. Higher values indicate higher inequality. GDP
per capita is adjusted for inflation and differences in living costs between countries.
Gini coefficient (plotted on a logarithmic axis)
Data source: World Bank Poverty and Inequality Platform (2026); Eurostat, OECD, IMF, and World Bank (2026)

Note: GDP per capita is expressed in
international-$
at 2021 prices. Depending on the country and year, inequality data relates to income

(measured after taxes and benefits) or to consumption,
per capita
. Where a country or region lacks data for the years shown, the closest
available value within 5 years is shown instead.
